question.text:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $G?$

  1. $(H \lor G) \land G$
  2. $H \land (H \lor G)$
  3. $(G \lor H) \lor G$
question.explanation:
The law that conjunction absorbs disjunction is stated as

\[ G \land (G \lor H) \equiv G. \]

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

  • Statement I is logically equivalent to $G.$ We have \[ \begin{align*} (H \lor G) \land G &\equiv G \land (H \lor G) \\[3pt] &\equiv G \land (G \lor H) \\[3pt] &\equiv G. \quad \color{green}\checkmark \end{align*} \]

  • Statement II is not logically equivalent to $G.$ We have \[ \begin{align*} H \land (H \lor G) &\equiv H \not\equiv G. \quad \color{red}\times \end{align*} \]

  • Statement III is not logically equivalent to $G.$ This statement cannot be simplified using the absorption laws.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

question.text:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $N?$

  1. $N \lor ( eg M \lor N)$
  2. $N \land ( eg M \lor N)$
  3. $( eg M \lor N) \land N$
question.explanation:
The law that conjunction absorbs disjunction is stated as

\[ N \land (N \lor \neg M) \equiv N. \]

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

  • Statement I is not logically equivalent to $N.$ This statement cannot be simplified using the absorption laws.
  • Statement II is logically equivalent to $N.$ We have \[ \begin{align*} N \land (\neg M \lor N) &\equiv N \land (N \lor \neg M )\\[3pt] &\equiv N. \quad \color{green}\checkmark \end{align*} \]
  • Statement III is logically equivalent to $N.$ We have \[ \begin{align*} ( \neg M \lor N) \land N &\equiv N \land (\neg M \lor N) \\[3pt] &\equiv N \land (N \lor \neg M) \\[3pt] &\equiv N. \quad \color{green}\checkmark \end{align*} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
